title: Day 5 Knowledge Check: End-to-End Grounded RAG

questions.question: Why is RAG preferred over parametric model memory for production SRE runbooks?

options.A: Runbooks change frequently; updating Qdrant JSON takes milliseconds without retraining weights, and citations prevent hallucinations.
options.B: Because LLMs cannot read English text without Qdrant.
options.C: Because RAG increases inference temperature to 2.0.

questions.explanation: RAG keeps dynamic operational knowledge externalized, auditable, and instantly updatable.
questions.implication: When an on-call engineer updates a rollback command, the next triage call immediately uses the new SOP.

questions.question: What happens if top_k is set too high (e.g., top_k=20) on a 1.5B SLM?

options.A: Irrelevant runbooks dilute attention ('Lost in the Middle'), increasing latency and confusion.

questions.explanation: Small context windows perform best with focused, high-precision Top-2 or Top-3 chunks.
questions.implication: Over-stuffing context degrades answer faithfulness and slows down CPU/GPU prefill latency.

questions.question: Which OpenTelemetry span kinds distinguish retrieval from generation in Arize Phoenix?

options.A: RETRIEVER for Qdrant search and LLM for model generation.

questions.explanation: OpenInference span kinds let you pinpoint whether an error came from bad retrieval or bad generation.
questions.implication: Separating retrieval metrics from generation metrics prevents wasting time tuning prompts when the real bug was a missing vector.
